evidence.description: Spec 083 FR-001; the registration surface exists only as invite redemption and the one-time first-run setup. Exercised by the Phase 2 acceptance script against staging: direct registration attempts (form posts without a code, code-shaped guesses) must all fail.

falsification_tests: Any account existing in the cloud identity store whose creation record is neither an invite redemption nor the first-run glassbreak setup; or a scripted registration attempt without a valid invite code that results in a created account or a usable session.
claims.text: No account can be created in the cloud edition except by redeeming a valid invite code or through the one-time first-run setup that creates the glassbreak admin. There is no open registration path.

evidence.description: Spec 083 FR-002; codes are CSPRNG-generated (>=128 bits), stored only as hashes in D1, carry an expiry (default 7 days), a single-use redemption flag, and a revocation flag; redemption is an atomic check-and-consume.

falsification_tests: Redeeming the same code twice (two accounts or two sessions from one code), redeeming a code after its expiry, or redeeming a revoked code, in any case succeeds.
A plaintext invite code found in the identity database, in any log, or in any repository file.
claims.text: Invite codes are single-use, expiring (default 7 days from creation), and revocable by an admin at any time before redemption; codes are stored only as hashes, and a code that is used, expired, or revoked can never create an account.

evidence.description: Spec 083 FR-003 + User Story 1; the deploy pipeline issues a one-time setup code (CSPRNG, single-use, 24-hour expiry) shown once to the deploying operator's terminal; the owner sets the glassbreak password himself on the setup screen; the setup route disables permanently once an admin exists.

Amendment 3 (owner, 2026-10-30): the glassbreak seed record carries the account email tristen.pierson@gmail.com as its contact identifier, and at go-live the one-time setup code plus the production URL are delivered to the owner as the glassbreak account prompt; the password is set by the owner on the setup screen and is never collected by the agent.

falsification_tests: The setup route accepting a code, or serving its form, after the glassbreak admin exists; or a second admin being creatable through the setup path.

The glassbreak password, or any reversible form of it, found in chat records, repository files, deployment logs, or pipeline artifacts (the salted password hash in the identity database is the only permitted residue).
claims.text: The glassbreak admin is seeded exactly once, through a first-run setup gated by a single-use setup code that expires within 24 hours; the owner chooses the password himself on the setup screen, and no password or password-equivalent ever passes through chat, code, configuration, or logs. After setup completes, the setup path is permanently closed.

evidence.description: Spec 083 FR-004; sessions are opaque CSPRNG tokens (>=256 bits) stored hashed in D1, carried in an HttpOnly + Secure + SameSite cookie; the only unauthenticated surfaces are the login, invite, setup, robots, and static shell-asset routes; logout and admin disable delete the session rows.

Amendment 2 (owner, 2026-10-30): with staging cancelled, the login wall is the deployment's stated protection, so FR-004 enumerates the anonymous surface and the falsifier enumerates the anonymous-access test, including a payload scan of anonymously fetched shell/assets against the desktop-resident dataset.

falsification_tests: Any data-bearing cloud route returning content to a request with no session, a forged session value, or an expired session.
A session belonging to a disabled or removed user continuing to authenticate after the disable/removal is recorded.
A session token readable from page JavaScript (cookie missing HttpOnly) or found unhashed in the identity database.

An anonymous request to any route outside the enumerated public surface (login, setup while open, invite acceptance, robots.txt, static shell assets) returning anything other than a redirect-to-login or a 401.

An anonymous fetch of the SPA shell or its assets whose payload contains project data - a dataset record, a workspace or program name drawn from the dataset, or a project count - as found by scanning anonymously fetched payloads against the desktop-resident dataset served through the hosted route.
claims.text: Every cloud-edition surface except login, invite redemption, the first-run setup (while open), robots.txt, and the static shell assets requires a valid user session; sessions are opaque, hashed at rest, cookie-carried with HttpOnly/Secure/SameSite, and are revoked immediately on logout, disable, or removal. The login wall is the deployment's protection (Amendment 2): for anonymous requests every other route returns a redirect-to-login or 401, and no project data - records, names, counts, or content-bearing payloads - is served anonymously in any form; the edge does not call the desktop origin for project data before authentication.

evidence.description: Spec 083 FR-015..FR-017 + Amendment 1's adopted access matrix (the conventional GitHub/Slack/Notion two-axis pattern): enforcement at the edge Worker for global/admin surfaces and at the desktop API for workspace scope, following Spec 081's scoped-404 pattern. The terminal is a global Admin/Owner facility in the cloud edition (D-5).

falsification_tests: A member session receiving anything other than 403 from any admin API, or anything other than a scoped 404 (with no workspace data) for a workspace the member holds no role in.
A member session successfully invoking the terminal, user management, invite management, workspace management, or any host-management action.
A Guest-type account holding, or being granted through any API, a per-workspace role above Viewer.
claims.text: Access is enforced on two axes on every request (Amendment 1): global user types (Owner - singular, the glassbreak account; Admin; Member; Guest, capped at Viewer) crossed with per-workspace roles (Owner/Admin/Member/Viewer/none), held independently per workspace. Admins manage users, invites, memberships, workspaces, and the terminal; members work only inside workspaces they hold a role in, see scoped 404s for workspaces they do not belong to, and cannot reach admin surfaces, other members' account data, or the terminal.

evidence.description: Spec 083 FR-006 as restated by Amendment 5: the hosted edition's data boundary is desktop residency. The publish pipeline (allowlist builder, marker scan, bundle, hydration) is retired; the edge's D1 store holds identity data only. Custody rule it mechanizes: statistics publishable, scans never redistributed.

Amendment 5 (owner, 2026-10-30): hosting moved to the owner's desktop; project data remains resident in the Spec 080 production install and is served in place through the edge/Tunnel route; no cloud dataset is created at any point.

falsification_tests: Any project or research artifact, restricted marker, restricted-source filename, or scan/preview image found in D1, Worker storage, Cloudflare configuration, or any other cloud-side store created for the hosted edition.

Any anonymous, unauthenticated, or workspace-unauthorized request receiving restricted or project content through the hosted route, or an authenticated session receiving restricted content outside the desktop application's existing restrictions.
A production dataset bundle, bundle store, or hydration path being created or used for the hosted edition.
claims.text: No cloud dataset exists in the hosted edition. Project and research data are resident only on TRISTEN-DESKTOP, in the Spec 080 production install; the edge stores only accounts, invite and session records, workspace-access records, setup state, and audit data. Restricted material (the CISI class: scans and their derivatives) is never copied into D1, Worker storage, a bundle store, or any other cloud storage, and can be returned through the hosted route only inside an authenticated, workspace-authorized member session under the desktop application's existing restrictions. (Restated by Amendment 5: the publish pipeline and its bundle boundary are retired.)

evidence.description: Spec 083 FR-007; the edge Worker sets X-Robots-Tag: noindex, nofollow on every response it passes (app pages, API responses, errors, static assets), and the app serves a robots.txt that disallows all paths; the login wall is the third layer. Owner order 2026-10-30: robots kept away until he lifts it.

falsification_tests: The standing header-check script finding any sampled response from either hostname (staging or production) — including an API error response and a static asset — without the X-Robots-Tag: noindex header, or a robots.txt that permits any path.
claims.text: Neither cloud hostname is indexable: every response carries X-Robots-Tag: noindex, nofollow, robots.txt disallows everything, and all data surfaces sit behind the login wall. This holds until the owner lifts it by name.

evidence.description: Spec 083 FR-008 as revised by Amendment 5; Spec 082's token continues to govern desktop installs and first-party automation only. In the hosted edition, browsers authenticate as users; the edge-to-desktop-origin service credential is a per-deployment secret held only in the Worker secret store and the desktop install's protected credential storage, injected by the edge on the VPC binding request, never rendered into any page, response, or client-visible configuration.

Amendment 5 SS2: the Workers VPC Service binding is the only origin path; its registered configuration (named tunnel, 127.0.0.1, port 8001) determines the target, and the edge calls it only after session termination and route authorization.

falsification_tests: Presenting a desktop install token to the cloud edge (as cookie, Authorization header, or query value) yielding any authenticated access.
The edge-to-desktop-origin service credential appearing in any client-visible response, page source, log line, or repository file.

The desktop application treating a request as a cloud member on the strength of X-Glossa identity headers presented without the valid service credential (for example, a direct request to 127.0.0.1:8001 with forged identity headers).

The desktop backend being reachable through any public route that bypasses the edge — a published Tunnel application for the hostname, a glossa CNAME to a cfargotunnel.com target, or any other alternate origin path.
claims.text: User sessions are the only browser credential in the hosted edition. The Spec 082 per-install token is never accepted by the cloud edge, and identity reaches the desktop origin only through the edge: the edge terminates the session, strips client-supplied identity headers, and injects the authenticated identity plus a per-deployment service credential onto the Workers VPC Service binding request carried by the named Cloudflare Tunnel. The desktop application accepts that identity only when the service credential validates; the credential exists only in the Worker secret store and the desktop install's protected credential storage — never in a page, a response, or the repository. (Revised by Amendment 5: the hop is edge to desktop origin.)

evidence.description: Architecture route study SS1/SS3/SS4: the hosted route serves the Spec 080 production desktop install itself (Amendment 5), which runs the same glossa_lab code and the same applied-epistemic-engineering library at the pinned >=1.5.0 line through the same aee_core adapter. The regression set is the GAP-ENV 23-claim set, including the five sign_val claims whose expected evidence value is 0.1625 under AEE 1.5.x (16 claims at that value).

falsification_tests: Any claim in the pinned regression set scoring differently through the hosted route than in local desktop use at the same AEE version, or the production desktop install resolving an AEE version outside the pinned >=1.5.0,<1.6 range.
claims.text: The cloud edition assesses claims with the same AEE library at the program's pinned version, through the same adapter code as the desktop app, so a claim's score means the same thing in both editions.

evidence.description: Spec 083 FR-010 as revised by Amendment 5; jobs execute in the resident engine of the desktop install, job state lives in the desktop-resident dataset, and the engine's stall semantics carry over — a job without heartbeat past the stall window is marked failed with the reason recorded — across ordinary desktop-backend restarts. No Cloud Run Job executions, service scale-to-zero, journal export, or scheduled cloud watchdog exists in this design.

falsification_tests: Stopping and restarting the desktop backend mid-job, or a job going without heartbeat past the stall window, leaves the job in a non-terminal 'running' state past that window, or the job's record vanishes from the desktop dataset.
A job submitted through the hosted route being executed by Cloud Run Jobs or by any other separate cloud execution venue.
claims.text: A job started in the hosted edition reaches a terminal state — completed, or failed with the reason recorded — across ordinary desktop-backend restarts. Jobs execute in the resident engine of the Spec 080 production desktop install and their state lives in the desktop-resident dataset; they are never delegated to a separate cloud execution venue, never silently lost, and never hang in a false 'running' state past the application's stall window. (Revised by Amendment 5: Amendment 4's Cloud Run Jobs model is retired; the guarantee is restated for the resident desktop engine.)

evidence.description: Spec 083 FR-011; the session identity is propagated from the edge into the desktop API and stamped on created/modified records (claims, digestion acts, study actions, anchor edits); surfaces render the actor's username. Digestion is by named humans (Spec 029 lane 2), so attribution is a correctness property, not decoration.

falsification_tests: Any claim, digestion act, or study action performed by a signed-in test member whose stored record lacks that member's user id, or whose surface rendering omits the actor.
claims.text: Every act performed in the cloud edition — registering or explaining a claim, a digestion act, running a study or job, editing anchors or data — is recorded with the acting user's identity and displays that attribution on the relevant surfaces.

evidence.description: Spec 083 FR-012; the audit log is a D1 table written by the edge for identity events and for hosted-route configuration events, append-only through the application (no update/delete path exists in the admin API), and viewable in the admin dashboard.

falsification_tests: Performing any listed action (login success or failure, invite create/redeem/revoke, role change, disable, removal, setup completion, hosted-route configuration change) and finding no corresponding audit entry with actor and timestamp.
An audit entry being modified or deleted through any application surface.
claims.text: Security-relevant events — logins (success and failure), invite creation/redemption/revocation, role changes, account disable/removal, the first-run setup, and hosted-route configuration changes — are written to an append-only audit log with actor and timestamp, readable in the admin dashboard and not editable through any application surface.

evidence.description: Amendment 5 (owner, 2026-10-30): hosting moved to the owner's desktop and no cloud dataset exists; the bundle/hydration machinery this claim governed (R2, then Google Cloud Storage) is retired from the design.

falsification_tests: A production bundle, manifest, bundle-store configuration, or hydration path for the hosted edition being created or used after Amendment 5.
The Status surface or the rollout record presenting a bundle id as the identity of the dataset being served, instead of the desktop install's revision/source commit and origin health.
claims.text: SUPERSEDED by Amendment 5 (2026-10-30): dataset versioning and atomic hydration are retired. No dataset bundle, manifest, bundle store, or hydration exists in the hosted edition, because project data is resident only on the Spec 080 production desktop install and is served in place through the edge/Tunnel route. The Status surface's bundle identity is replaced by the desktop install's revision/source commit and origin-health state (FR-013 as superseded; replacement tasks T057/T060). This claim is retained so the retirement is on the record, not silently dropped.

evidence.description: Amendment 2 (owner, 2026-10-30): staging is cancelled - the login wall is the protection - so verification runs against local production-shaped builds and ephemeral preview deployments, the proof battery runs before the production deploy, and go-live follows the proofs directly.

Amendment 5 (owner, 2026-10-30): the single production route is the Worker Custom Domain at glossa.bitconcepts.tech backed by the named desktop Tunnel and its Workers VPC Service; the go-live gates are Spec 080 cutover-final, the BitConcepts Cloudflare write/configuration scopes, and the desktop cloudflared service installation through Desktop Access.

falsification_tests: A staging hostname resolving, or staging resources existing for this edition at any time — on Cloudflare (a staging Worker, D1 database, Tunnel, or VPC Service), on the desktop route, or in any Google Cloud Run service, job, or storage bucket created for this edition.
A glossa CNAME to a <UUID>.cfargotunnel.com target, a published Tunnel application for glossa.bitconcepts.tech, or any public route reaching the desktop backend except through the edge Worker.

The production route being opened for member use, or the glassbreak setup being completed, before the pre-launch proof record (claim-test results as amended, the C083-6 cloud-storage audit, the adversarial pass, the noindex checks, and the desktop-offline and bypass proofs) exists in the rollout record.
claims.text: Rollout is production-only (Amendment 2; decision D-7 cancelled): exactly one public hosted route exists, at glossa.bitconcepts.tech — a Worker Custom Domain whose edge reaches the desktop origin only through the named Tunnel's Workers VPC Service — and no staging hostname or staging resources are ever created. There is no published Tunnel application or cfargotunnel.com CNAME for the hostname, and no second public origin or bypass route to the desktop backend. The full flow is proven against a production-shaped local build and ephemeral preview deployments, and the route-specific proof battery (T059) passes on the assembled production route before it is opened for member use or the glassbreak setup prompt is issued; go-live follows the proofs directly and is recorded in the rollout record. (Revised by Amendment 5; Amendment 4's Google venue is retired and its go-live gate is dead.)

evidence.description: Spec 083 FR-015 + Amendment 1 SS1, mechanism as revised by Amendment 5: the primary workspace's scope assignment is verified in the desktop-resident dataset (task T057), with the reconciliation report comparing counts per resource class against the desktop dataset itself.

falsification_tests: Any resource in the desktop-resident dataset lacking a workspace assignment, or assigned in the initial scope reconciliation to any workspace other than the primary workspace.
The scope-reconciliation report's count for any resource class differing from the desktop dataset's count for that class.
Any unscoped project resource being served through the hosted route.
claims.text: Before the hosted route opens, a primary workspace named 'Indus Script' exists in the desktop-resident dataset and holds all existing project state: every project resource in the Spec 080 production desktop dataset is assigned to that workspace, the scope-reconciliation report's per-class counts match the desktop dataset's own counts exactly, and no resource is ever served unscoped through the hosted route. (Mechanism revised by Amendment 5: assignment is verified in the desktop dataset, replacing the first-publish mechanism.)

evidence.description: Spec 083 FR-016 + Amendment 1 SS1/SS4 (decision D-1 applied: workspace creation is an admin act); the admin Workspaces tab is wireframe 09.

falsification_tests: A Member- or Guest-type account creating or archiving a workspace through any route or API.
Any surface of an archived workspace returning content to a non-admin user.
claims.text: Only global Admin and Owner accounts can create or archive workspaces. An archived workspace serves nothing: every one of its surfaces answers scoped 404 to non-admin users.

evidence.description: Spec 083 FR-017 + Amendment 1 SS2's adopted matrix (per-workspace Owner/Admin/Member/Viewer), enforced at the edge and in the desktop API, which binds scoped queries to the identity's entitled workspace ids itself.

falsification_tests: A Viewer-role user mutating any content in that workspace, or a Member-role user changing workspace membership or settings, through any route.
A user exercising, in a second workspace, powers that derive only from a role they hold in a first workspace.
claims.text: A user's effective powers inside a workspace are exactly their per-workspace role, with global Admin/Owner holding implicit Workspace Admin: Viewers cannot mutate workspace content, Members cannot manage workspace membership or settings, and a role held in one workspace confers nothing in another.

evidence.description: Spec 083 FR-017 + Amendment 1 SS3: workspace scope is carried by every resource, queries and aggregates (search, lists, counts, badges, the switcher) are computed inside the viewer's memberships, closing the badge-scoping gap recorded in Spec 081's closeout.

falsification_tests: Any response to a user lacking a role in workspace W - including search results, list payloads, counts, and badges - containing any of W's resource identifiers, titles, or counts.
A direct request by such a user for any enumerated resource class of W returning anything other than a scoped 404 with no data.
claims.text: No cross-workspace leakage exists in any form: a user without a role in a workspace receives a scoped 404 for every resource class of that workspace (workspaces; claims and their records including digestion; evidence and sources; anchor sets and data surfaces; studies; experiments and analysis runs; jobs and results; discovery items; research-loop sessions; notebooks; reports; foundation status), and that workspace contributes nothing to their search results, lists, counts, or badges.

evidence.description: Spec 083 FR-017 + Amendment 1 SS4: the per-user workspace-access matrix (wireframe 10) reads and writes the same grant store the enforcement path reads, and role changes revoke sessions immediately (FR-004), so an edit is effective on the next request.

falsification_tests: The access view showing a workspace grant that does not exist in the identity store, or omitting one that does.
An access edit (grant, role change, or revocation) made in the dashboard not being reflected in the target user's enforcement on their next request.
claims.text: The admin dashboard's per-user workspace-access view is accurate and effective: it displays exactly the grants stored for that user (no phantom grants, none missing), and an edit made through it is the enforcement reality on the target user's next request.
